source_citation: Underlying manuscript transcriptions ('ED Material') are from the Emily Dickinson Archive, a partnership of Amherst College Archives & Special Collections, Houghton Library at Harvard University, and other holding institutions (edickinson.org / curiosity.lib.harvard.edu), based on The Poems of Emily Dickinson: Variorum Edition, ed. R.W. Franklin (1998). Per EDA's own Copyright & Terms of Use (https://curiosity.lib.harvard.edu/emily-dickinson-archive/about/copyright-terms-of-use), ED Material is licensed CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 and used here under its personal/non-commercial-research provision, with credit to the owning institution as required -- the specific owning institution for each leaf of Fascicle 34 should be confirmed from EDA's own per-item credit line before any use beyond that. Felix Oke separately deposited a working scrape of this data on Zenodo for preservation (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10316549, labeled CC-BY-4.0 there) -- that more permissive label applies to the deposit as an act of preservation, not as a relicensing of the underlying ED Material, which remains governed by EDA's own NC-ND terms above.
note_on_this_file: Contains only short base-text/variant phrase pairs extracted from <add type="alternate" extent="...">...</add> markup, not full poem transcriptions, images, or apparatus -- the full TEI corpus and its images are kept out of this repository entirely, used only locally for this non-commercial research, per EDA's own terms above.
corrections_to_earlier_rounds: Poem 3 ('A little Road- not made of Man'): earlier (round 2) reconstruction from a published reading-edition text had the base/variant direction backwards for one pair. TEI confirms: base 'Curricle' -> variant 'Vehicle' (not the reverse as previously stated).

Poem 6 ('So much Summer'): earlier reconstruction guessed base 'should' -> variant 'could', misreading an unmarked word. TEI confirms the actual marked pair is base 'Would' -> variant 'Could -', a different word in the poem. The team's own hand-documented 'Extravagant' and 'importunate' variants for 'exorbitant' are NOT present in this TEI transcription at all -- kept as team-observed-only data, not TEI-confirmed (see note below).

Poem 11 ('No Bobolink- reverse His Singing'): round 2 guessed 'Root' -> 'Core' from position notes and semantic plausibility. Direct inspection of the TEI shows NO variant markup at 'Clove to the Root' at all. This pair is RETRACTED as unconfirmed and likely incorrect. The TEI's actual marked pair at that stanza is base 'Best' -> variant 'All' (matching the team's own list item 'all', previously left unplaced).

missing_markup_finding.summary: Cross-checking the team's own 2022 hand-documentation against this project's scraped TEI files finds poems 1 ('Bereavement...') and 5 ('Pain- has an Element of Blank') have ZERO <add type="alternate"> markup, despite the team hand-documenting real variants for both (3 variants for poem 1, in Table 1 of the paper draft; 1 variant, 'time'->'Day', in the Fascicle 34 documentation). Poem 2 ('I think to Live- may be a Bliss') gives the clearest quantified measure: of the team's 13 hand-documented pairs (Table 1), 11 (85%) match the TEI exactly; 2 ('Bliss'->'Life' and a second 'but been'->'bleak' variant) are absent from this project's scraped files.
missing_markup_finding.likely_cause: An earlier draft of this note called this an 'archive completeness gap,' implying the Emily Dickinson Archive's own transcription work was incomplete -- that's not well-supported and was corrected. The TEI Consortium's own project description of EDA states that capturing Dickinson's emendations via the critical-apparatus module was an explicit encoding goal, not an afterthought. The more likely explanation is this project's own 2022 data pipeline: the TEI files were pulled by custom Python scraping, built because 'there was no API for the original EDA' (per this repo's own README) -- exactly the kind of process that can miss content inconsistently across items. This hasn't been confirmed against the live archive either way, so it's stated as the more plausible explanation, not a settled claim about EDA's scholarship.
missing_markup_finding.implication: Whatever the cause, it's a real, quantifiable gap in what THIS project holds versus what the team saw firsthand on the manuscripts -- worth knowing before treating this project's own scraped TEI as a complete record of Fascicle 34's variants.

classification_summary.round_1_source: Team's own Table 1 worked example (16 pairs, both poems 1 and 2), validated against team-assigned labels
classification_summary.round_2_source: 9 pairs verified against published reading-edition texts (before TEI access), first-pass classification, no ground truth
classification_summary.round_3_source: 31 pairs verified directly against TEI <add type="alternate"> markup across 9 more poems, first-pass classification, no ground truth
classification_summary.combined: 22 of 56 pairs across three independent rounds and all 17 Fascicle 34 poems that have any documented variants (56%, 33%, 32% respectively) -- the 'substitutive' gap is not an artifact of any one round or poem; it is the single largest relationship type the formal five-category taxonomy has no defined category for.
